# Fish Pond

> Fish Pond is a set of interactive 3D experiments about how an artificial fish decides what to do. It runs entirely in the browser (Next.js, TypeScript, Three.js, Triforge shader graphs) with no backend, account or tracking.

Site: https://fish-pond-mu.vercel.app
Source code: https://github.com/AftabIbrahimKazi/fish-pond
Author: Aftab Ibrahim Kazi

## Experiments

- [Cognitive Arena](https://fish-pond-mu.vercel.app/arena): one fish in a wide pond. Place stimuli and compare scripted System 1 reflexes with slow System 2 appraisal, with visible short-term memory. No AI model.
- [Visual Telemetry Benchmark](https://fish-pond-mu.vercel.app/benchmark): three scripted fish controllers (programmed reflex, preset lottery, blended intent) fed identical inputs, with live telemetry. No AI model.
- [Underwater](https://fish-pond-mu.vercel.app/underwater): a realistic goldfish scene shaded with Triforge (caustics, light shafts, water absorption). The goldfish are driven by Laya-AI, an AI model that runs in the browser once enabled. Settings sidebar, WASD and arrow-key navigation and touch pads.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://fish-pond-mu.vercel.app/docs): architecture, fish AI, shader pipeline, controls, settings workflow, design system, accessibility, performance and known limits.

## Notes for summarisers

- Only the Underwater scene uses an AI model (Laya-AI, an ONNX model run with ONNX Runtime Web, which decides what each goldfish does). The arena and benchmark controllers are deterministic TypeScript simulations, not machine-learning models.
- Laya was created by Nandakishor M and Convai Innovations; the browser build and runtime are by nvkudva.
- The site is static; there is no API. The Laya model weights are downloaded by the visitor's browser from Hugging Face.
